USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Use the early-October talks to test whether Beijing will convert this week's farm-exemption and purchase signals into enforceable commitments, without adding new tariffs or walking back the existing Section 301/Huawei posture. Keep List 3 at 25% and List 4A at 15% as leverage, leave the Oct 15 hike (25%→30% on ~$250B) and Dec 15 List 4B contingent on progress, and do not trade away entity-list or structural IP/tech-transfer demands for a purchase-only package. A two-week goodwill delay is enough of a gesture; further unilateral rollback now would surrender leverage just as China is showing it needs a pause.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is real but not existential. The dispute has moved from industrial lists onto consumer goods (List 4A at 15% on ~$110–125B effective Sept 1) and China has retaliated on ~$75B including autos, while US farm exports remain the main hostage. August already showed the domestic cost: Michigan sentiment collapsed from 98.4 in July to 89.8 in August, ISM manufacturing fell to 49.1 (first contraction since 2016) with export orders cited as the trade-war channel, the 10-year yield sank to 1.47% and the 2s10s inverted, VIX spiked to 24.59 on Aug 5 after the manipulator designation, and the Fed has already cut (fed funds 2.42%→2.04%). That is material GDP/political drag—especially in the farm belt Democrats attacked at the Sept 12 debate—but it is not a supply-chain or ally-cohesion crisis, and CPI remains contained. Offset: China is also under pressure (CNY through 7, US designation as manipulator, pork/ASF inflation, IP growth cooling to the mid-4s) and has just offered the first tariff-exemption list plus soy/pork exclusions and reported soybean cargoes. Structural issues that blew up the May text (enforcement, IP, tech transfer) remain unresolved, so this is not a moment of US advantage that justifies another hike, nor a collapse that justifies concession. Action should therefore sit at negotiate: talks are scheduled, both sides just exchanged small goodwill moves (US delay of the Oct 1 hike to Oct 15 at Liu He's request; China farm exemptions), and escalating again would likely replay August's market/sentiment shock while conceding purchases or rolling back tariffs before a matching structural offer would waste the remaining leverage.
key_factors: List 4A now live on consumer goods; Oct 15 hike and Dec 15 List 4B still hanging
August macro stress: ISM contraction, sentiment crash, yield-curve inversion, VIX spike, Fed cut
Farm-belt exposure to Chinese retaliation vs. this week's soy/pork exemption and purchase inquiries
Structural IP/enforcement/Huawei issues unresolved after May breakdown and empty Shanghai round
China also strained (CNY >7, manipulator label, pork inflation) and signaling it wants a pause, not a settlement
October talks are the right venue; further unilateral escalation or rollback would be mistimed

CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Engage the October Washington round and the working-level meetings without new structural commitments or a further tariff/entity-list spiral. Keep the existing retaliatory architecture in place, use limited farm-purchase authorizations and the 16-category exemption list as reversible goodwill, and press for a matching U.S. delay or rollback of the October 15 hike and December 15 List 4B. Do not lock in large purchase quotas or IP/SOE reforms until the U.S. puts concrete tariff relief on the table.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high but not existential. Since May the U.S. raised List 3 to 25%, put Huawei and dozens of affiliates on the Entity List (expanded again 21 Aug), designated China a currency manipulator after CNY broke 7, and on 1 Sep put List 4A (~$110–125B) into force at 15%, with List 4B still hanging over phones/laptops/toys (timeline 2019-05-10 through 2019-09-01). That maps to the CHN +0.5 anchor: export sectors hit, Huawei firm-level targeting, FX pressure. Official August activity confirms the bite — industrial output +4.4% YoY, a 17½-year low, with delivered industrial exports down 4.3% (Reuters 16 Sep); PPI in deflation; CPI pushed by a 47% pork spike from African swine fever. DEXCHUS weakened from ~6.71 in April to 7.08 on 18 Sep. Offsetting that, reserves are stable near $3.11T, merchandise exports have not collapsed, and mid-September goodwill (China’s first exemptions 11 Sep; soy/pork exclusions and soybean cargoes 13 Sep; Trump’s two-week delay of the next hike) has reopened a talks path. Escalating now would likely invite the delayed Oct 15 hike and Dec 15 List 4B and deepen the industrial slump; a large unrequited concession would repeat the May collapse over enforcement/structural text. Negotiation with small, reversible agricultural gestures is the stance that matches a +0.45 threat: stop the next tariff wave, buy time on Huawei/tech, and keep structural red lines off the table until there is a matching U.S. offer.
key_factors: List 3 at 25% plus List 4A at 15% already live; List 4B still scheduled for 15 Dec
Huawei Entity List plus August affiliate expansion remains the core tech/sovereignty threat
CNY through 7 and U.S. manipulator designation; reserves still ~$3.11T
August industrial output at a multi-year low and export deliveries falling
Pork/ASF food-price pressure creates a domestic reason to allow some U.S. farm imports
Reciprocal mid-September goodwill and Liu He–Lighthizer October round make talks the live option
Further Chinese escalation would likely trigger the delayed U.S. October hike and December List 4B
